title: The higher derived functors of the adequacy functor vanish on module-valued functors
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file adequate.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: With the notation of the chapter's injective-object lemma, the assertion is that R^p Q(F) = 0 for p > 0 and every adequate functor F (statement lines 1590-1595). The proof replaces F by a three-term resolution whose terms are module-valued functors and applies the two-term spectral sequence for a composition of functors, reducing the claim to R^p Q(M-underlined) = 0 for a plain module; it then argues by contradiction: a nonzero R^i Q(M-underlined) means the kernel of Q(I^i) -> Q(I^{i+1}) is strictly larger than the image of Q(I^{i-1}), the surjection lemma provides a linearly adequate L mapping into that kernel without factoring through the image, adjointness transfers the map to I^i and hence produces a nonzero element of Ext^i_P(L, M-underlined), contradicting the vanishing lemma (proof lines 1597-1623). The level is H3: a spectral-sequence reduction followed by a genuinely argued contradiction, with both the reduction and the adjointness step displayed.
